summary: Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held an attested post at the City University of Hong Kong in 2018.

Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme, and held positions at Tübingen (attested 1988), Zurich (1990), Freiburg (attested 2001), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served at the University of Michigan, where he was attested as co-director in 1980 and affiliated in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy from around 1782 to 1784, Jesus College, Cambridge in 1784, and the University of Cambridge from circa 1784 to 1788.

Thomas Roebuck was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School. He served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811 and was a member of The Asiatic Society.
Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his B.A. studies at Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and Queen's University of Ireland (~1857–1861).
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD from the University of Zurich, where he studied under Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, with John Dewey, and earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, Dorje Pamo Monastery, and under several teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama. She held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Sravasti Abbey.

Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Nyima and Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).

Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught numerous figures, including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Thubten Samphel was a Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College and the University of Delhi (~1973–1977), as well as Columbia University (~1981–1982). He served at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thubten Yeshe was a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery and under Geshe Rabten, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, and Zong Rinpoche. He founded several organizations and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Yeshe and the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded several centers and served as spiritual director of the FPMT beginning in 1984.

Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned a Geshe Lharam at Ganden Shartse and a B.A. from Cambridge. He held posts at Ganden, Girton College, Stanford, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics, which he founded.
Thupten Tsering is a scholar in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology. He has held academic posts at Tibet University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.
Thushini S. Jayawardena is a scholar of religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka and earned a PhD from Auckland University of Technology by 2017.

Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and later taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1953–1957) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (~1964–1975).

Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and completing his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1967–1977).
